transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-09
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lara Chen (Nova CISO), Marcus Doyle (Eng Manager), Evan Park (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focusing on SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Nova is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for a chat + embeddings product, wants clarity on compliance artifacts and integration steps. Next: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs, SAML metadata, schedule SE technical deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey all, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account, with Priya, our SE. Lara, Marcus, Evan, thanks for making time. Quick agenda — understand your security requirements and where Redwood fits (hosted, dedicated, private), answer any questions, and agree next steps.

[00:20] Lara Chen: Thanks Samir. Quick intro from our side — I'm Lara, CISO. We run security for Nova, we handle vendor assessments. Marcus is our eng manager leading the LLM rollout, Evan handles infra and SSO. Primary asks: SOC 2, ISO status, how SSO/SAML and RBAC work, and what audit logs you provide. Also curious about encryption and KMS/HSM options and retention/deletion.

[00:40] Marcus Doyle: Also want to understand the performance tradeoffs — we're leaning Hosted for speed but may need Dedicated for data isolation. Can you explain where Redwood Hosted stores customer data and how long logs are kept?

[01:05] Priya Nair: Sure — high level, Redwood Hosted keeps customer data in encrypted storage; we support region selection for data residency, and we have SOC 2 Type II and an ISO 27001 attestation (we can share the summary and auditor report). We also offer Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) with tenant isolation, and Private deployments for VPC/on-prem where you control networking and keys.

[01:30] Evan Park: When you say "control keys" in Private, do you mean customer-managed KMS/HSM? How does the runtime access model keys for ephemeral inference?

[01:50] Priya Nair: For Private, yes — you can plug in your KMS or HSM; the control plane can be customer-managed. For Dedicated and Hosted we offer KMS integration: for Hosted we use our managed KMS but support envelope encryption with customer-wrapped keys and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for enterprise plans. There are different levels — key wrapping, HSM-backed storage, and rotation policies. The inference runtime performs in-memory decryption for model weights and KV cache, then discards ephemeral keys. (Note: sometimes automation docs say "KV cash" in transcriptions — it's KV cache).

[02:20] Lara Chen: OK. We need proof points: SOC 2 report, ISO summary, penetration test results if you have them. Also, audit logs — do you provide immutable audit logs for admin actions, API calls, and data access? Format? Retention?

[02:45] Samir Patel: Yes — we provide audit logs for control plane actions, API requests (token-level metadata), and admin UI events. Logs are exportable as newline-delimited JSON or CSV, and we can push to customer-owned S3 or to a SIEM via secure forwarding. Default retention on Hosted is 90 days, but enterprise and Dedicated can get longer retention (365+), and Private you decide retention policies. We can also provide hashed events for immutability and signed log chains on request.

[03:20] Marcus Doyle: How about RBAC and SSO? We need SAML 2.0 for SSO and role mappings tied to LDAP groups. Is that supported out of box?

[03:40] Priya Nair: Yes, SAML 2.0 and SCIM are supported. You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles (admin, billing, developer, viewer). We integrate with common IdPs — Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace — and support custom SAML metadata. SCIM provisioning is available on enterprise plans for automatic user sync and group sync.

[04:00] Evan Park: Any gotchas for SAML when using Dedicated or Private? We run our own IdP inside the VPC.

[04:15] Priya Nair: For Private, since the control plane can be customer-managed in your VPC, you point the SAML endpoints internally; we provide an example metadata XML and a guide for ephemeral cert rotation. For Dedicated, SAML typically routes through the Redwood control plane but we can configure a SSO tunnel or federated SAML depending on your network. We'll document options in the integration guide.

[04:40] Lara Chen: Data residency — we have EU customers, need to guarantee data stays in EU for certain tenants. Can Hosted guarantee region-level isolation?

[04:55] Samir Patel: Yes, we support region pinning for Hosted; you can choose EU regions for storage and inference. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where workloads are pinned to specific GPUs in the chosen region. We'll include the region controls and network diagrams in the docs.

[05:20] Marcus Doyle: Auditability around model versions — we want history of which model versions served which requests, to trace regressions. Do you track model version metadata in logs?

[05:35] Priya Nair: We do. Every request has model id, model version, and route id in the token-level logs. The Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, and you can export time-series or raw logs for forensics.

[05:50] Lara Chen: Retention and deletion: if a user exercises GDPR right to be forgotten, how does Redwood handle deletion of inference logs and training data?

[06:10] Samir Patel: Good question. For Hosted, we have API and Console controls to purge customer data and to exclude logged prompts from any downstream training. We keep system logs necessary for security for a minimum audit period, but PII removal can be run on demand; we have deletion workflows and can provide attestations. For Private, retention is under your control. We'll share our data retention policy template.

[06:40] Evan Park: Is there an option to disable request logging entirely? For some tenants we'd prefer no prompt persistence.

[06:50] Priya Nair: Yes, on Dedicated and Private you can disable request logging or enable only hashed request fingerprints. Hosted can be configured with request redaction and no-training flags per request. There's an account-level setting and an API header to set 'x-redwood-no-log' for sensitive calls.

[07:10] Marcus Doyle: Encryption in transit and at rest — standard TLS? How about database encryption and backups?

[07:25] Priya Nair: We use TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit. At rest, storage volumes and object stores are encrypted (AES-256), and snapshots/encrypted backups use our KMS or customer's KMS depending on plan. We also support HSM-backed key wraps for highest assurance.

[07:45] Lara Chen: Pen test cadence and bug bounty?

[07:50] Samir Patel: We have an annual third-party pen test and a private bounty program for enterprise customers; we can share summary findings and remediation timelines.

[08:05] Lara Chen: For procurement, our security questionnaire needs to be filled — we usually use a spreadsheet. Will you fill ours or do you provide a security questionnaire export?

[08:20] Samir Patel: We typically provide a completed questionnaire for SOC2/ISO items and a security pack with answers. For bespoke questionnaires we'll need some time but we can do it as part of the sales process.

[08:35] Marcus Doyle: On dedicated performance — if we choose Dedicated, how does failover work if a GPU node goes down? Any automatic fallback to Hosted?

[08:50] Priya Nair: Dedicated pools have autoscaling and redundancy; if capacity is constrained we can configure policy-based fallback to compatible model variants on Hosted or other capacity tiers, but that requires agreement in the SLA and network/trust setup. We can also run cross-zone replicas depending on your availability needs.

[09:15] Evan Park: What about logging for privileged actions — UI admin changes, keys rotations — can we get immutable, tamper-evident logs?

[09:30] Priya Nair: Yes, we support write-once log exports and can sign logs for tamper evidence; for Private deployments you can host the log collector. We also provide alert hooks for unusual admin actions.

[09:50] Lara Chen: How long to get SAML set up? Our IdP team is small.

[09:58] Samir Patel: Typically 2-5 business days to exchange metadata and test SSO, depending on IdP. We'll send SAML metadata and the quickstart SSO guide after this call.

[10:10] Marcus Doyle: On the audit logs export — do you have a sample export we can look at? Column names for model id, request id, timestamp, user id, route id?

[10:25] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll attach a sample NDJSON export and a mapping of fields.

[10:35] Lara Chen: Any special compliance for embedding vectors — can vectors be treated as PII? We need guidance on policies if vectors are considered sensitive.

[10:55] Samir Patel: We treat embeddings as data; governance is customer-specific. We recommend observing the same retention and access controls as other sensitive data; for Hosted, you can opt out of vector retention or enable encryption-at-rest with separate keys. We'll add a note to the PII guidance.

[11:15] Marcus Doyle: Timeline wise, we're looking to start a POC in ~4 weeks and hope to be in prod in 3 months if procurement clears. Any recommended path?

[11:30] Samir Patel: Recommended: start with a Hosted trial to validate integration and performance (low lift), then move to Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity for isolation, and consider Private if you need strict network controls or on-prem. We'll propose a POC plan with benchmarks and success criteria.

[11:50] Lara Chen: Can you summarize the differences in terms of compliance and control between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private?

[12:05] Priya Nair: Short summary: Hosted = fastest onboarding, Redwood-managed keys/ops, region pinning, enterprise contracts for BYOK and longer retention. Dedicated = reserved capacity, stronger tenant isolation, enterprise SLAs, more custom KMS integrations. Private = customer-managed control plane, full network control (VPC), customer KMS/HSM, best for regulated/adverse environments. We'll send a one-pager.

[12:35] Evan Park: Any blocker around our requirement to have audit logs forwarded to our SIEM in real time?

[12:45] Priya Nair: No blocker — we support secure log forwarding (TLS) or S3 export; for real-time streaming we can integrate with your Kafka or a push to SIEM via our connector. We'll include config examples.

[13:05] Lara Chen: Great. Any red flags on your side about our timeline/requirements?

[13:15] Samir Patel: Nothing major — main thing is to finalize which deployment mode (Hosted trial vs Dedicated pilot). For SSO and audit exports you're covered; we'll follow up with the docs.

[13:30] (brief cross talk)

[13:45] Samir Patel: Recap / next steps: we'll send SOC 2/ISO docs, SAML metadata, sample audit log export, architecture diagram, and a proposed POC plan with benchmarks. Priya will schedule a SE-led deep dive next week. Action items on the doc.

[14:10] Lara Chen: Sounds good. We'll send our security questionnaire and the list of EU regions we need.

[14:25] Marcus Doyle: I'll sync with Evan on exact throughput numbers — roughly 3-5M tokens/day for initial rollout, peak 10M/day. We'll include model types (chat + embeddings).

[14:40] Evan Park: I'll provide the IdP point of contact for SSO.

[14:50] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone, appreciate the time. We'll follow up by EOD with the doc pack and a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.

[15:00] End of recording.
